headline.headline: DIAMONDBACKS SURVIVE 12-INNING MARATHON IN PITTSBURGH, 8-7
headline.deck: Arizona escapes PNC Park after Pirates rally from six down in final two innings
headline.body:
PITTSBURGH — The Arizona Diamondbacks needed every one of twelve innings to escape PNC Park with an 8-7 victory over the Pittsburgh Pirates on Tuesday night, surviving a stunning Pittsburgh comeback that turned a comfortable six-run lead into a white-knuckle extra-inning thriller before a crowd of 19,024.

Arizona built its advantage steadily, scoring in the first, second, third, fourth and sixth innings to carry a 6-0 lead into the late stages. The Pirates, however, erupted for three runs in the eighth and three more in the ninth to knot the game at seven and send it to extras. The game remained deadlocked through the tenth and eleventh before the Diamondbacks pushed across the decisive run in the twelfth. Corbin Carroll, who was hit by a pitch from Gerson Soto during the contest, was among the central figures in Arizona's attack through the long night. Nolan Arenado had a runner take his spot in the tenth inning after reaching base.

The four-hour, one-minute affair was the kind of summer grind that defines pennant races. The Diamondbacks, sitting third in the NL West at 54-53 after the game, avoided what would have been a catastrophic collapse and kept pace in a crowded divisional chase. The Pirates fell to 42-66 with the defeat, their late-game explosion not enough to complete one of the more dramatic comebacks of the 2026 season.

secondary.headline: GUARDIANS SPLIT SERIES WITH REDS, WIN OPENER 6-5
secondary.deck: Manzardo homer and Burns' pitching lift Cleveland in game one; Cincinnati takes nightcap 2-0
secondary.body:
CINCINNATI — The Cleveland Guardians and Cincinnati Reds split their Tuesday doubleheader at Great American Ball Park, with Cleveland winning the opener 6-5 before the Reds took the nightcap 2-0 in front of 26,928 fans. In the first game, Kyle Manzardo launched his 12th home run and DJ Stewart added his 22nd as Cleveland scored four runs in the first inning and held on despite a four-run Cincinnati fourth that tied the game. Chandler Burns earned the win. Stephenson Lowe contributed a double for the Guardians, who got an insurance run in the eighth.

The evening belonged to Cincinnati starter Gavin Williams, who shut out Cleveland over nine innings in the nightcap, allowing the Reds to salvage a split of the day-night affair. Cade Halpin was hit by a pitch from Junior Garcia, and Manzardo was plunked by Tejay Antone in the second game. The rubber match of the series goes Wednesday, with Cleveland sitting second in the AL Central at 55-54 and Cincinnati fifth in the NL Central at 50-56.

secondary.headline: LEONARD WILLIAMS IN CONTRACT TALKS WITH SEAHAWKS AS TRAINING CAMP OPENS
secondary.deck: Pro Bowl defensive lineman and Seattle in active negotiations on a new deal
secondary.body:
RENTON, Wash. — Pro Bowl defensive lineman Leonard Williams confirmed Tuesday that his representatives and the Seattle Seahawks have entered contract discussions, injecting a significant storyline into the opening days of the team's 2026 training camp. Williams, one of the most disruptive interior pass rushers in the NFC, would represent a cornerstone piece for a Seattle defense looking to reassert itself heading into the new season.

The Seahawks camp has been generating considerable buzz on multiple fronts, with quarterback competition and position battles drawing attention from coaches and scouts. Adding Williams to the mix on a long-term deal would signal Seattle's intention to build around its defensive front. No agreement had been announced as of Tuesday, but the two sides were described as actively engaged in conversations.

secondary.headline: GRANATO STEPS BACK: CANUCKS SHIFT HALL OF FAMER TO ADVISER ROLE
secondary.deck: Cammi Granato moves from assistant GM position in a quiet but notable Vancouver front-office shake-up
secondary.body:
VANCOUVER — The Vancouver Canucks announced Tuesday that hockey Hall of Famer Cammi Granato is transitioning out of her assistant general manager role and into an advisory position within the organization, a front-office restructuring that arrives in the middle of the NHL's second-round playoff action. Granato had been widely praised as a trailblazing executive presence in a league that has seen slow growth in women's front-office leadership.

The timing of the shift, with the Canucks organization navigating both the offseason roster rebuild and the ongoing league-wide free agency period that opened June 30, drew immediate attention across hockey circles. Granato's move to an adviser role raises questions about the direction of Vancouver's front office at a pivotal moment in the franchise's competitive window. The Canucks have not elaborated publicly on the scope of her new responsibilities.

column.headline: PITTSBURGH'S COLLAPSE SHOULD HAUNT THE PIRATES ALL SUMMER
column.body:
Six runs. The Pirates had six runs to play with heading into the eighth inning Tuesday night, and they handed the entire pile back to Arizona before the ninth was finished. That is not a pitching failure or a defensive miscue — that is an organizational statement. A team that cannot protect a six-run lead against any opponent in late July is telling the baseball world exactly who it is, and right now Pittsburgh is telling a grim story.

The Diamondbacks deserve credit for refusing to quit through twelve innings and four hours of baseball. But the real story out of PNC Park is what the Pirates did to themselves. At 42-66, they are already deep in a lost season. Blowing that kind of cushion does not just cost a game — it costs a clubhouse its confidence. Pittsburgh's front office faces hard questions about whether this roster is being built or simply endured.

story.headline: TIGERS DEMOLISH ORIOLES 14-0 AS KREMER STIFLES BALTIMORE THROUGH EIGHT INNINGS
story.deck: Detroit scores in every frame but the ninth to hand Baltimore a humiliating shutout loss.
story.body:
DETROIT, July 28 — The Detroit Tigers sent the Baltimore Orioles home battered and scoreless Tuesday night, rolling to a 14-0 rout at Comerica Park before 27,453 fans as pitcher Kremer controlled the Orioles lineup from the first pitch to the final out. Detroit struck for two runs in the opening frame and never stopped, piling up runs in eight consecutive innings before the ninth to hand Baltimore one of its most lopsided defeats of the season.

Torres powered the Tigers offense with a home run and a double, while Valencia added a solo shot — his fourth of the year — as Detroit finished with 14 runs on a relentless assault that stranded 17 runners and could have been worse. Zach McKinstry contributed a double, Javier Baez added one of his own, and Colt Keith turned in a triple as the Tigers worked through the Baltimore pitching staff with consistent damage in every corner of the lineup.

The loss dropped the Orioles to 52-56, firmly lodged in fourth place in the American League East, while Detroit climbed to 51-57 in the AL Central. The Orioles could manage only 10 runners left on base, a testament to how thoroughly Kremer and Detroit's bullpen shut down any threat Baltimore mounted over the course of the 2-hour, 27-minute contest.

story.headline: DRAYMOND RETURNS: GREEN AGREES TO ONE-YEAR DEAL TO STAY IN GOLDEN STATE
story.deck: The veteran forward re-signs with the Warriors for $27.7 million, setting up a pivotal 2027.
story.body:
Draymond Green is staying home. The four-time NBA champion and defensive anchor agreed Tuesday to return to the Golden State Warriors on a one-year, $27.7 million deal, according to league sources, keeping intact one of the most recognizable partnerships in recent basketball history. Green, who turns 36 in March, chose to bet on himself and the Warriors organization rather than test a market that offered longer-term security elsewhere.

The decision ends weeks of speculation about whether Green would finally part ways with the franchise that drafted him in the second round back in 2012. His return gives head coach Steve Kerr a proven defensive enforcer and a floor general whose IQ and intensity remain elite despite the advancing years. Green averaged 8.6 points, 7.2 rebounds and 6.0 assists last season, numbers that barely hint at the chaos he creates on the defensive end and the culture he reinforces in the locker room.

Insiders familiar with the negotiations suggest the one-year structure was entirely deliberate, positioning both Green and Golden State for what one league source called a 'huge' 2027 offseason. With Stephen Curry entering the final chapters of his career and the Warriors still hunting a fifth championship banner, Green's short-term commitment keeps the organization flexible while ensuring the team's heartbeat stays on the floor for at least one more run at glory.

story.headline: BLUE JACKETS LOCK UP SILLINGER, GREAVES AS COLUMBUS BETS BIG ON YOUTH
story.deck: Columbus avoids arbitration, signs two cornerstones in a busy Wednesday in the NHL.
story.body:
The Columbus Blue Jackets made their most emphatic statement of the offseason Wednesday, securing two of their most important young players on the same day and signaling that the franchise's long rebuild is shifting into a new gear. Forward Cole Sillinger agreed to a three-year, $13.875 million deal to avoid arbitration, while goaltender Jet Greaves inked a three-year, $15 million contract running through the 2028-29 season. Together, the two signings give Columbus a pair of under-25 pillars locked in at critical positions as the organization pushes toward sustained contention in the Metropolitan Division.

Sillinger, 22, has developed steadily since being selected 12th overall in the 2021 draft, and the Blue Jackets made clear they had no interest in letting a hearing determine his value. Greaves, who emerged as one of the more compelling goaltending stories of the past two seasons, now carries the burden of becoming a franchise netminder in a market starved for playoff hockey. At $5 million per year, the organization is betting Greaves has the temperament and athleticism to handle that weight night after night.

Elsewhere around the league, former Philadelphia Flyers coach John Tortorella told reporters Wednesday he was disappointed by the Vegas Golden Knights' decision not to retain him following their surprising postseason run, but said he remains motivated to find his next bench job. In Vancouver, Hockey Hall of Famer Cammi Granato is transitioning from assistant general manager to an adviser role within the Canucks' front office, a shift the organization framed as a natural evolution of her contributions to the club.

story.headline: DRAFT DARLINGS AND DOLLAR SIGNS RESHAPE THE NFC AS MAY MINICAMP BUZZ BUILDS
story.deck: Rookie contracts signed, veteran shuffles complete as teams finalize rosters for summer camps.
story.body:
The ink is barely dry on a flurry of rookie deals across the league, and already the chatter from team facilities is loud enough to rattle goalposts. The Chicago Bears, riding momentum from their second-round selection of Oklahoma linebacker Marcus Tillman, agreed to terms with the 22-year-old on a four-year, fully guaranteed rookie contract Tuesday, giving defensive coordinator Alan Williams a sideline weapon with the speed to cover tight ends and the instincts to blitz off the edge. Tillman ran a 4.51 forty at the combine and posted 14 sacks in his final college season, numbers that had scouts from 11 franchises requesting private workouts before April's draft.

On the veteran market, the Dallas Cowboys made the loudest splash of the week by trading disgruntled receiver Darius Conwell to the Pittsburgh Steelers in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick and veteran cornerback Jameel Whitfield. Conwell had requested a trade in March after failed extension talks, and Dallas owner Jerry Jones confirmed the deal at a brief press availability Wednesday, calling it a move that gives both sides a fresh start. Whitfield, 28, fills an immediate need at corner for a Cowboys secondary that surrendered 24 touchdown passes last season.

Looking ahead, the New England Patriots are generating the most training camp intrigue of any franchise after signing former Los Angeles Rams quarterback Devon Straker to a two-year, $54 million deal in early April. Head coach Jerod Mayo refused to name a starter at Tuesday's organized team activities, insisting the competition between Straker and third-year signal-caller Preston Hobbs remains genuinely open. Hobbs threw for 2,900 yards and 18 touchdowns in 2025 but also led the AFC in interceptions, and Patriots brass clearly wants pressure applied before pads go on in late July.
